claims.statement: Predefined container-image annotation keys may describe the image, its asserted license and its source repository. Metadata labels are not verified provenance, accepted license permission, complete attribution or per-file distribution rights; the fragment does not enumerate keys or establish an actual image.

GraphQL may delete a private package version only for certain registries. The inspected include excludes granular-permission registries from the GitHub Packages GraphQL API and points to registries supporting only repository-scoped permissions. This is not universal deletion capability, actual registry identification, sufficient permission or authorized deletion; linked permission matrices remain separate review work.

Packaging after build/test may create runnable/deployable artifacts for local tests, users or staging/production. Java mvn package, Node container, Maven Central and NuGet examples are illustrative and were not executed. Workflow artifact downloads differ from package-registry publication; a screenshot caption is not inspected image or real artifact receipt. Publishing to GitHub Packages on default-branch pushes is optional advice, while release-triggered publication is another pattern, not a mandatory universal trigger. Product variables resolve GitHub Packages and GitHub; no package creation, installation, upstream code execution, publication, deployment, rights clearance or approval is implied. Linked introduction/release guides remain separate review work.

Actions workflow configuration varies by package client. A general workflow-authoring pointer is not a complete client adapter, valid package-auth configuration or executed workflow; the pinned Actions variable identifies GitHub Actions and the linked guide is not reviewed by reference.

The containing package flow calls for placing .npmrc in its repository so GitHub Packages can locate the project. The fragment does not specify contents or authorize committing credentials; project configuration must not be treated as permission to expose tokens. No .npmrc was written, secret accessed or package published; the file-addition guide remains separate review work.

In the GHES branch, a described package type may be unavailable because site administrators may enable or disable each supported type. This is not live capability discovery, a universal entitlement, successful operation or permission to activate disabled features; the containing type and linked enterprise configuration require further context.
